Sha is a flower gathered from the heaths, scrublands and moors of cold north-western Endor. It remains extremely difficult to find in its natural habitat.

The flowers are dried and ground into powder, with ingestion listed as the preparation’s method of use. The powder allows the user to see up to about 300 feet in almost complete darkness for 10–50 rounds. A painful bout of diarrhoea often follows several hours later. Repeated use can cause habituation.
